days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday starts out at the Intervale, where Fair Share needs volunteers from 2:30 to 6:30 to help run the free CSA that feeds over 350 families, and helpers can take home produce while it lasts. The Elks Lodge on North Avenue gets its weekly Monday Night Bingo going at 4:30 with a $1,000 jackpot game, and Pearl Street Pub in Essex Junction hosts its free Monday Night Open Mic at 6. At 7, Burlington's play reading group The Neighbors opens its 137th season at a home on North Prospect Street, where guests sit in the audience while members read a surprise play, so email ahead to reserve a seat. Also at 7, pickup dodgeball at the Miller Center needs no team, just $5 a game, Underdog Pinball runs its Target Matchplay tournament at The Archives, and the Forever 38 crew heads to Essex Cinemas for Verity [MEETUP] , the new Colleen Hoover adaptation with Dakota Johnson and Anne Hathaway. Nashville singer songwriter Katie Pruitt brings her Fools for the Fleeting Tour to the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge at 7:30, with Next of Kin opening.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday starts early. Vermont's tech crowd gathers over waffles and coffee at Zero Gravity for Tech Tuesdays breakfast [MEETUP] from 8 to 10, and The Network of Women hosts its monthly networking coffee for women at Hula at 8:30. From 9 to noon, Common Roots in South Burlington wants volunteers to plant next season's garlic, with fall treats to share after. At 5, French speakers and learners meet at Burlington Bay Market & Café for Pause-Café Mardi , and Fletcher Free Library hosts Writing for Healing , a drop in hour of meditation and writing with no experience needed. From 6 to 8, Dad Guild starts Mending Men , a new monthly workshop at the Soda Plant where dads and masculine identifying caregivers learn visible mending from Sophie Hood of Little Bird Sewing Studio, RSVP required, while the library's Crafters Drop-In welcomes anyone with a knitting, crochet or embroidery project. Main Street Landing's free classic film series shows 'Pet Sematary' at the Film House at 7. At 7:30 the big shows split up, with Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee Ann Wilson of Heart , the voice behind "Barracuda" and "Crazy on You," at the Flynn and Canadian vintage pop band Bombargo in the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge. Dancers can finish the night at North Star Community Hall, where Vermont Swings hosts its weekly DJ dance from 8 to 9:30.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday means our own Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] back at Gutterson for indoor hoops at 5:30 ($12 day pass) so come get some runs in. Earlier in the day, Queen City Cat Lounge on North Avenue adds a morning cat yoga class at 10 with the adoptable cats and kittens, capped at eight so sign up first, and Skirack opens gear intake for its Winter Swap from 10 to 6 through Friday, so fill out the online form before dropping off your used winter gear on Main Street. At 5, Tibetan scholar and Dalai Lama translator Geshe Thupten Jinpa talks about finding happiness through gratitude at St. Michael's College, free, and the Vermont Green Building Network gathers at Four Quarters in Winooski for Building Science and Beer , free with registration. At 6, Bluehouse Group hosts ChatBTV [MEETUP] , quick talks and demos on what's working with AI with food and drinks provided, Old Spokes Home teaches a one night bike care clinic ($37.50-$60) covering flats, wheels and drivetrain care, and Phoenix Books' Trash for the Trope book club takes on Kate Clayborn's Georgie, All Along. At 6:30, VTIFF unveils this year's lineup at its free festival preview at the Main Street Landing Film House, with light bites from Bramble first, and Vermont Comedy Arts holds its $5 improv night at the Vermont Comedy Club with an open jam after. Adventure Dinner in Colchester screens the PBS film Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World at 7, opening with a reading by Vermont poet laureate Bianca Stone, and Lily's Pad on North Avenue hosts its free open mic and community potluck from 7 to 10.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday gets going in Shelburne, where OLLI's Why Birds Sing talk with Lisa Zinn runs from 1:30 to 3 at St. Catherine of Siena Church Hall, with registration closing Wednesday. ArtSpark's Creative Cousins , a free BIPOC centered open mic, runs from 5 to 7 at Pingala on North Avenue, and everyone is welcome to listen. In the Old North End, the monthly ONE Community Dinner serves a special Eritrean and Ethiopian meal from guest chef Mulu Tewelde from 5:30 to 6:30 at 20 Allen Street, with curried lentils, spicy mushrooms and injera, free with donations welcome and everyone invited. It's a great way to meet your neighbors. Over on North Street, the Peace & Justice Center's Solarpunk Book Club & Game Night starts at 5:30, and Wild Meadows Books in Williston hosts a bring your own project Craft Night from 6 to 8. Goose drummer Cotter Ellis leads improvised sets recorded live in front of a small audience at Tank Recording Studio for Cotter & Friends at 6 and 8, and New York comic David Drake starts a four show run at the Vermont Comedy Club at 6:30. At 7, the Burlington-Honfleur Sister Cities Committee screens The Mystery of Satie free at BCA Studios with filmmaker Bastien Loukia there in person, Cirque Alfonse brings La Noce to the Flynn, a 1970s wedding party told through acrobatics and live music, and Standing Stone Wines in Winooski hosts Make It a Monologue , a free open mic for monologues. Benjamin Tod & Lost Dog Street Band close out the night in the Higher Ground Ballroom at 8:30, with Candi Jenkins opening.
